# Models

Meta ships seven model lines. [Muse Wonder](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/models#muse-wonder), [Muse Spark](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/models#muse-spark), [Muse Ember](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/models#muse-ember), [Muse Image](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/models#muse-image), [Muse Voice Transcribe](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/models#muse-voice-transcribe), and [Segment Anything Model (SAM)](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/models#sam-3) are hosted on Meta Model API; [Muse Glimmer](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/models#muse-glimmer) is open-weight and runs on your own hardware. Muse Spark also has an open-weight release, [Muse Spark Open](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/models#muse-spark-open). Pick one by what you're building, then read its section to learn more. To decide between Muse Wonder, Muse Spark, and Muse Ember, see [Choose a model](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/choose-a-model).

## Models at a glance

| Use case                                                              | Model                                                                                                                                                                          | Input                              | Output               | API endpoints                                                                                                                                                                               |
| :-------------------------------------------------------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :--------------------------------- | :------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Agentic work, coding, and reasoning                                   | [Muse Wonder](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/models#muse-wonder), [Muse Spark](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/models#muse-spark), [Muse Ember](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/models#muse-ember) | Text, image, video, audio, and PDF | Text                 | [Responses](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/protocols/responses), [Chat Completions](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/protocols/chat-completions), [Messages](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/protocols/messages) |
| Image generation and editing                                          | [Muse Image](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/models#muse-image)                                                                                                                       | Text and image                     | Image                | [Responses](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/protocols/responses), [Image generation](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/image-generation)                                                                    |
| Speech to text                                                        | [Muse Voice Transcribe](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/models#muse-voice-transcribe)                                                                                                 | Audio                              | Text (transcription) | [Transcribe](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/speech-to-text)                                                                                                                                       |
| Image and video segmentation                                          | [Segment Anything Model](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/models#sam-3)                                                                                                                | Text prompt, image, and video      | Text (geometry)      | [Responses](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/protocols/responses), [Segmentation](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/sam/overview)                                                                            |
| Self-hosted or provider-hosted agentic and coding work; post-training | [Muse Spark Open](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/models#muse-spark-open)                                                                                                             | Text, image, video, and audio      | Text                 | None ([self-host](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-spark-open/deploy) or a [hosted provider](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-spark-open/deploy#hosted-providers))                                |
| Self-hosted inference; supervised fine-tuning                         | [Muse Glimmer](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/models#muse-glimmer)                                                                                                                   | Text and image                     | Text                 | None ([self-host](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-glimmer/deploy))                                                                                                                            |

> **NOTE: Availability by country**
>
> Model availability can vary by country. See the [Geographic Use Policy](https://dev.meta.ai/legal/geographic-use-policy) for country-specific restrictions.

## Muse Wonder

Muse Wonder is Meta's most capable model, built for complex software engineering and long-horizon agentic work. It makes and verifies changes across many files in real repositories, and it plans, delegates to sub-agents, calls tools in parallel, and recovers from errors across many steps. Muse Wonder is in preview.

| Model ID          | Input                          | Output | Context window   |
| :---------------- | :----------------------------- | :----- | :--------------- |
| `muse-wonder-1.0` | Text, image, video, audio, PDF | Text   | 1,048,576 tokens |

Muse Wonder comes in two variants: Muse Wonder on Model API and in [Muse Code](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code), and the higher-capability Muse Wonder Full in Muse Code only. See the [Muse Wonder](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-wonder) page for specs, recommended settings, and availability.

## Muse Spark

Muse Spark is Meta's model for agentic and coding work at scale, such as multi-step tool loops, software engineering assistants, and long-context reasoning. It comes in three versions, and Muse Spark 1.3 is recommended for new work.

| Model ID                                             | Input                          | Output | Context window   |
| :--------------------------------------------------- | :----------------------------- | :----- | :--------------- |
| `muse-spark-1.3`, `muse-spark-1.2`, `muse-spark-1.1` | Text, image, video, audio, PDF | Text   | 1,048,576 tokens |

On Model API, Muse Spark also offers discounted Contributor-mode variants. See the [Muse Spark](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-spark) page for every version, recommended settings, and availability.

## Muse Ember

Muse Ember is the efficient execution model in the Muse family, built for high-volume, repeated work: sub-agent tasks, tool calls, routing, and processing large collections of images, files, and records. It takes the same requests as Muse Spark at a lower price per token. Pair it with Muse Spark or Muse Wonder: the larger model plans, and Muse Ember handles the volume.

| Model ID         | Input                          | Output |
| :--------------- | :----------------------------- | :----- |
| `muse-ember-1.0` | Text, image, video, audio, PDF | Text   |

On Model API, Muse Ember runs in Standard mode only. See the [Muse Ember](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-ember) page for specs, recommended uses, and availability.

## Muse Image

Muse Image is Meta's image generation model line. Send a text prompt (and optional reference images) and get an image back, or send an image with an instruction to edit it. One model handles both generation and editing. It's agentic, so it can search the web for visual references and current facts and run code to build layouts before it renders.

| Model ID         | Input       | Output |
| :--------------- | :---------- | :----- |
| `muse-image-1.0` | Text, image | Image  |

Reach Muse Image two ways: the [Responses API](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/protocols/responses) for conversational, multi-turn editing, or the single-shot [`/v1/images/generations`](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/api-reference/images/create-image) and [`/v1/images/edits`](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/api-reference/images/edit-image) endpoints for one-off calls. See the [Image generation](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/image-generation) guide to get started.

## Muse Voice Transcribe

Muse Voice Transcribe is Meta's speech-to-text model on Meta Model API. Use it to transcribe live audio streams or supported audio files.

| Model ID                    | Input | Output          |
| :-------------------------- | :---- | :-------------- |
| `muse-voice-transcribe-1.0` | Audio | Text transcript |

Muse Voice Transcribe is built for real-time speech products: voice agents, meeting and call intelligence, live transcription, dictation, captioning, and high-volume transcription. It supports streaming speaker diarization, native endpointing and voice activity detection, contextual and keyword biasing, 25 evaluated languages with code-switching, and turn-level timestamps.

It returns transcript text. It does not synthesize speech or provide a speech-to-speech conversation API. It does not provide word-level timestamps, sound event detection, or emotion detection.

Reach Muse Voice Transcribe two ways: the realtime WebSocket endpoint (`wss://api.meta.ai/v1/asr/realtime`) for live audio, or the file endpoint ([`POST /v1/asr/transcribe`](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/api-reference/voice/transcribe)) for a recording you already have.

Start with the [Muse Voice Transcribe guide](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/speech-to-text). See [Pricing and rate limits](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/pricing-rate-limits#muse-voice-transcribe-pricing) for audio pricing.

## Segment Anything Model

SAM 3.1 is Meta's segmentation model on Meta Model API. Give it a short noun phrase such as "yellow school bus" with an image or video, and it returns every match as a box and a pixel-accurate mask. Or mark specific objects with boxes, points, or masks to segment only those objects. One model handles both stills and clips, and in video it follows each object across frames.

| Model ID  | Input                     | Output          |
| :-------- | :------------------------ | :-------------- |
| `sam-3.1` | Text prompt, image, video | Boxes and masks |

Reach SAM 3.1 over the [Responses API](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/protocols/responses) ([`POST /v1/responses`](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/api-reference/responses/create-response)), and upload clips through the [Files API](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/file-handling) when you segment them more than once. See the [SAM overview](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/sam/overview) to get started.

## Muse Spark Open

Muse Spark Open is the open-weight release of Muse Spark: an 816B-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 42B active parameters. You don't call it over Model API. Download the weights and serve them through a runtime such as SGLang, vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, or llama.cpp, or call it through a hosted inference provider.

Muse Spark Open lives in the [Open-weight models](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/open-weight-models) section:

- **[Muse Spark Open overview](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-spark-open)**: checkpoints, hardware, license, and launch partners.
- **[Get the model](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-spark-open/get-the-model)**: download the BF16 or NVFP4 weights.
- **[Run inference](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-spark-open/deploy)**: serve it on your own GPUs or call a hosted provider.
- **[Post-training](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-spark-open/post-training)**: adapt it with supervised fine-tuning (SFT) or reinforcement learning (RL).

## Muse Glimmer

Muse Glimmer is Meta's open-weight multimodal model, distilled from Muse Spark and built to run on your own hardware. You run it yourself instead of calling it over Model API: download the weights and serve them through a runtime such as vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, or ExecuTorch.

Muse Glimmer lives in the [Open-weight models](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/open-weight-models) section, covering how to get, prompt, deploy, and customize the model:

- **[Muse Glimmer overview](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-glimmer)**: variants, architecture, license, and launch partners.
- **[Get the model](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-glimmer/get-the-model)**: download the weights and verify your setup.
- **[Run inference](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-glimmer/deploy)**: pick a runtime and serve it locally.
- **[Post-training](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-glimmer/post-training)**: adapt it to your domain with supervised fine-tuning (SFT) or reinforcement learning (RL).

## List models via the API

Query the catalog programmatically when you need to check what's enabled for your team. This returns the API-hosted models; self-hosted Muse Glimmer isn't included.

**Python (OpenAI SDK)**

```python
import os

from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://api.meta.ai/v1",
    api_key=os.environ["MODEL_API_KEY"],
)

response = client.models.list()

print(response.model_dump_json(indent=2))
```

**TypeScript (OpenAI SDK)**

```typescript
import OpenAI from 'openai';

const apiKey = process.env.MODEL_API_KEY;
if (!apiKey) {
  throw new Error('MODEL_API_KEY is not set');
}

const client = new OpenAI({
  baseURL: 'https://api.meta.ai/v1',
  apiKey,
});

const models = await client.models.list();

console.log(JSON.stringify({ object: models.object, data: models.data }, null, 2));
```

**Python (requests)**

```python
import json
import os

import requests

response = requests.get(
    "https://api.meta.ai/v1/models",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['MODEL_API_KEY']}"},
)
response.raise_for_status()
print(json.dumps(response.json(), indent=2))
```

**curl**

```shell
curl -X GET "https://api.meta.ai/v1/models" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MODEL_API_KEY"
```

The response returns models sorted newest-first by creation time, with the model ID as a stable tiebreaker. Each object includes a `created` field — the Unix timestamp in seconds for when the model was added to the registry. `GET /v1/models/{model}` returns the same `created` value for a single model.

- [Pricing and rate limits](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/pricing-rate-limits): per-token rates for Standard and Contributor mode, and rate limits for each model
- [Subscriptions](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/subscriptions): Muse Code plans and what each one includes
pricing:
# Pricing and rate limits

Use our models with pay-as-you-go billing on Meta Model API and in [Muse Code](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code), or in Muse Code with a monthly [subscription](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/subscriptions). This page covers pay-as-you-go: Model API bills the reasoning models (Muse Wonder, Muse Spark, and Muse Ember) per token, image generation per image, Muse Voice Transcribe by the hour of audio processed, and Segment Anything Model (SAM) per image or video frame segmented, with no minimums or upfront commitment.

## Pricing modes

Some models can be used in two modes. Standard mode uses standard pricing. Contributor mode offers discounted pricing or more usage in exchange for permission to use your content — the prompts, code, files, and context you send, plus the model responses you get back — to train future Meta models.

### Standard mode

In Standard mode, you pay standard prices and your content is not used to train Meta models. Every model on this page is available in Standard mode.

### Contributor mode

On Model API, Contributor mode runs the same models at heavily discounted token prices, in exchange for permission to use your content to train future Meta models. It lowers the barrier to entry for prototyping, testing integrations, and scaling experiments where it's acceptable for Meta to use your content to train future Meta models.

On Model API, use Contributor mode with Muse Spark 1.3 or 1.2 by calling its Contributor-mode variant: `muse-spark-1.3-contributor` or `muse-spark-1.2-contributor`. Contributor mode isn't available for Muse Wonder or Muse Ember on Model API.

In [Muse Code](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code), subscriptions default to Contributor mode, and you can turn it on or off in settings; see [Contributor mode in Muse Code](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/subscriptions#contributor-mode).

## Model pricing

### Muse Wonder

Model: `muse-wonder-1.0`.

| Usage        | Contributor mode (per 1M tokens) | Standard mode (per 1M tokens) |
| :----------- | :------------------------------- | :---------------------------- |
| Cached input | Not available                    | $0.20                         |
| Input        | Not available                    | $4.00                         |
| Output       | Not available                    | $20.00                        |

### Muse Spark

Models: `muse-spark-1.3`, `muse-spark-1.2`, and `muse-spark-1.1` in Standard mode; `muse-spark-1.3-contributor` and `muse-spark-1.2-contributor` in Contributor mode. Muse Spark 1.1 is Standard mode only.

| Usage        | Contributor mode (per 1M tokens) | Standard mode (per 1M tokens) |
| :----------- | :------------------------------- | :---------------------------- |
| Cached input | $0.002                           | $0.15                         |
| Input        | $0.10                            | $1.25                         |
| Output       | $0.20                            | $4.25                         |

### Muse Ember

Model: `muse-ember-1.0`, in Standard mode only.

Muse Ember has two price tiers, and the input tokens in your API request set the tier, cached tokens included. When a request continues a stored conversation with `previous_response_id`, its input includes that conversation. A request with up to 200K input tokens is billed at the rates in the first column. A request with more is billed at the long-context rates in full, not only for the tokens past 200K. Your invoice and usage dashboard list the two tiers separately.

| Usage        | Up to 200K input tokens (per 1M tokens) | Over 200K input tokens (per 1M tokens) |
| :----------- | :-------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------- |
| Cached input | $0.004                                  | $0.012                                 |
| Input        | $0.10                                   | $0.30                                  |
| Output       | $0.50                                   | $1.50                                  |

### Token pricing notes

These apply to the reasoning models above.

- **Cached input costs less**: When part of your prompt matches a [cached prefix](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/prompt-caching), you pay the cached-input rate for those tokens. Check `cached_tokens` in the response to see how many were served from cache.
- **No long-context premium on Muse Wonder and Muse Spark**: you pay the same rate whether your context window is mostly empty or almost full. Muse Ember bills requests with more than 200K input tokens at higher rates; see [Muse Ember pricing](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/pricing-rate-limits#muse-ember-pricing).
- **Web search grounding**: **$2.50 per 1,000 search queries**, in addition to the request's token cost. This applies to the [`web_search` tool](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/search-grounding) on the reasoning models, [Muse Wonder](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/models#muse-wonder), [Muse Spark](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/models#muse-spark), and [Muse Ember](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/models#muse-ember).

> **NOTE: Muse Image search is included**
>
> [Muse Image](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/models#muse-image)'s built-in web and image search is part of its per-image price and isn't charged separately. See [Muse Image pricing](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/pricing-rate-limits#image-generation).

### Muse Image

| Usage           | Price           |
| :-------------- | :-------------- |
| Generated image | $0.01 per image |

[Muse Image](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/models#muse-image) is billed at a flat rate per generated image. The price is the same regardless of prompt length, `reasoning_strength`, or the tools the model uses during generation, including its built-in web and image search, which isn't charged separately. A request that returns `n` images is billed for `n` images. You're billed only for images the model successfully generates and returns: images that fail to generate, or that are removed by safety filtering before they're returned, aren't counted. Image responses still include a `usage` object with token counts for reference, but image generation tokens are not included in token-based pricing for other models. See the [Image generation](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/image-generation#images-response) guide for the response shape.

### Muse Voice Transcribe

[Muse Voice Transcribe](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/speech-to-text) is billed by audio processed, metered in whole seconds.

| Usage           | Price          |
| :-------------- | :------------- |
| Audio processed | $0.18 per hour |

Streaming and non-streaming transcription are priced the same. Zero data retention (ZDR) is priced at parity with Standard mode. Contributor mode isn't available for Muse Voice Transcribe. Audio time is billed as a separate line item from token usage, rounded down to whole seconds; other endpoints aren't billed for audio time.

### Segment Anything Model 3.1

[SAM 3.1](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/models#sam-3) segmentation is billed per image and per video frame, not per token. The same prices apply to streaming and non-streaming requests. Each video request is billed for at least 50 frames, so a clip or tracking range shorter than 50 frames is billed as 50. The response's `usage.video_frames_processed` reports the frames billed for that request.

| Usage              | Price                  |
| :----------------- | :--------------------- |
| Image segmentation | $2.50 per 1,000 images |
| Video segmentation | $0.20 per 1,000 frames |

## Rate limits

Rate limits apply **per team, not per API key**: requests, tokens, and streams from every key in a team count toward the same limits. Each model below has its own limits, so traffic to one model doesn't use up another's.

| Model                        | Requests per minute (RPM) | Tokens per minute (TPM) | Other limits                                    |
| :--------------------------- | :------------------------ | :---------------------- | :---------------------------------------------- |
| `muse-wonder-1.0`            | 3,000                     | 4,000,000               |                                                 |
| `muse-spark-1.3`             | 3,000                     | 4,000,000               |                                                 |
| `muse-spark-1.2`             | 3,000                     | 4,000,000               |                                                 |
| `muse-spark-1.3-contributor` | 150                       | 3,000,000               |                                                 |
| `muse-spark-1.2-contributor` | 150                       | 3,000,000               |                                                 |
| `muse-spark-1.1`             | 3,000                     | 4,000,000               |                                                 |
| `muse-ember-1.0`             | 3,000                     | 4,000,000               |                                                 |
| `sam-3.1`                    | 3,000                     | None                    |                                                 |
| `muse-image-1.0`             | 150                       | None                    |                                                 |
| `muse-voice-transcribe-1.0`  | None                      | None                    | 256 concurrent streams; 16,000 streams per hour |

[SAM 3.1](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/models#sam-3) is [billed per image or frame](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/pricing-rate-limits#sam-pricing) and [Muse Image](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/models#muse-image) is [priced per image](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/pricing-rate-limits#image-generation), so neither has a TPM limit.

[Muse Voice Transcribe](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/speech-to-text) is [billed by audio processed](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/pricing-rate-limits#muse-voice-transcribe-pricing), so it's limited by streams rather than requests or tokens. **Concurrent streams** caps how many transcription sessions you hold open at once; **streams per hour** caps how many you start. Realtime and file transcription share the same budget.

Token usage counts only **your** input and output tokens. Meta injects a small amount of steering context into every prompt (a system prompt and related scaffolding); those injected tokens are not billed and are excluded from the token counts reported in your `usage` and by the [token-counting endpoints](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/prompt-caching#injected-tokens).

### Background responses

Creating [background responses](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/protocols/responses#using-with-other-features) (`background: true`) is limited to **600 submissions per minute, per team**, in addition to the limits above. The cap applies only to starting new background responses: over it, new submissions return `HTTP 429 Too Many Requests` with a `Retry-After` header, and responses already running continue unaffected.

## Handle rate limits

When you exceed a limit, the API rejects the request. Requests succeed again once usage drops below the limit.

### Retry on 429 responses

**Retry strategy:** Use exponential backoff with jitter. Start with a short delay such as 500 ms, double it after each consecutive rate-limit response, and add random jitter so concurrent clients don't all retry at the same moment. If the response includes a `Retry-After` header, wait at least that long.

### Read rate-limit headers

Every successful token-based response includes headers that report your current limit and remaining quota:

| Header                           | Description                                  |
| :------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------- |
| `x-ratelimit-limit-tokens`       | Total token budget for the current window.   |
| `x-ratelimit-remaining-tokens`   | Tokens remaining before you hit the limit.   |
| `x-ratelimit-limit-requests`     | Total request budget for the current window. |
| `x-ratelimit-remaining-requests` | Requests remaining before you hit the limit. |

Read these headers and slow down before you hit a rate limit instead of reacting after one.

### Handle Muse Voice Transcribe rejections

A realtime stream rejected for exceeding a stream limit closes with `1013`. A rejected file-transcription request returns `HTTP 429 Too Many Requests`. Transcription responses don't include the `x-ratelimit-*` headers.

- [Models](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/models): every model line, with links to each model's versions and availability
- [Subscriptions](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/subscriptions): Muse Code plans, an alternative to pay-as-you-go
families:
# Muse Wonder

Muse Wonder is Meta's most capable model, built for complex software engineering and long-horizon agentic work. It makes and verifies changes across many files in real repositories, and it plans, delegates to sub-agents, calls tools in parallel, and recovers from errors across many steps, following detailed instructions closely.

> **NOTE: Preview**
>
> Muse Wonder is in preview. For more about the model, see the [Muse Wonder model page](https://dev.meta.ai/models/muse-wonder) and the [Muse Wonder model card](https://research.meta.ai/static/muse-wonder-model-card).

## At a glance

|                                                            |                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| :--------------------------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Model ID**                                               | `muse-wonder-1.0`                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **Input**                                                  | Text, image, video, audio, and PDF                                                                                                                                                          |
| **Output**                                                 | Text                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **Context window**                                         | 1,048,576 tokens                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **[Reasoning effort](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/reasoning)** | `"minimal"` to `"max"`; the default is `"max"`                                                                                                                                              |
| **Endpoints**                                              | [Responses](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/protocols/responses), [Chat Completions](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/protocols/chat-completions), [Messages](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/protocols/messages) |
| **Pricing**                                                | Pay-as-you-go, Standard mode only; see [Muse Wonder pricing](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/pricing-rate-limits#muse-wonder-pricing)                                                              |
| **Rate limits**                                            | See [rate limits](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/pricing-rate-limits#rate-limits)                                                                                                                 |

## Build with Muse Wonder

Use Muse Wonder when capability matters more than cost per token:

- **Multi-file coding changes**: make and verify changes across many files in a real repository.
- **Long-running agents**: plan, delegate to sub-agents, and work through multi-hour runs with parallel tool calls.
- **Agent main loops**: run the main loop of a [coding agent](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/coding-agents) or an [agent framework](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/agent-frameworks), and hand lower-cost subtasks to [Muse Ember](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-ember).
- **Computer use**: drive a desktop from screenshots with the native [computer use](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/computer-use) tool.

Muse Wonder also handles [image understanding](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/media-understanding#images), [video](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/media-understanding#video) and [audio](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/media-understanding#audio) understanding, [tool calling](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/tool-calling), [structured output](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/structured-output), and [search grounding](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/search-grounding). For high-volume, latency-sensitive, or cost-sensitive work, see [Choose a model](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/choose-a-model).

## Set reasoning effort

Muse Wonder supports every [reasoning effort](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/reasoning) level from `"minimal"` to `"max"`. For agentic coding, start with `"high"`. Save `"xhigh"` and `"max"` for the hardest problems, such as tracing a concurrency bug or planning a large migration, where a correct answer matters more than speed.

On Model API, `"max"` on `muse-wonder-1.0` doesn't select Muse Wonder Full, which is available only in Muse Code.

## Make your first call

Muse Wonder takes the same requests as Muse Spark on the same endpoints. Follow the [quickstart](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/quickstart#first-call) and set the model to `muse-wonder-1.0`. Most examples in these docs that use `muse-spark-1.3` run on Muse Wonder with that change; [Switch between models](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/choose-a-model#switch-models) lists the settings that differ.

## Availability

Muse Wonder comes in two variants. Muse Wonder is on Model API and in [Muse Code](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code). Muse Wonder Full, the higher-capability variant, is available only in Muse Code with a subscription, so setting reasoning effort to `"max"` on Muse Wonder doesn't select it.

| Variant                         | Model API (pay-as-you-go)      | Muse Code                                                                                                                                                       |
| :------------------------------ | :----------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Muse Wonder (`muse-wonder-1.0`) | Available (Standard mode only) | Pay-as-you-go and [every plan](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/subscriptions#about)                                                                          |
| Muse Wonder Full                | Not available                  | [Power Usage](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/subscriptions#power-usage) and [Maximum Usage](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/subscriptions#maximum-usage) |

With a subscription, Muse Wonder is available on every plan and Muse Wonder Full on the Power Usage and Maximum Usage plans, each in [Standard mode](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/pricing-rate-limits#standard-mode) and [Contributor mode](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/pricing-rate-limits#contributor-mode).

Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full aren't currently available in South Korea, on Model API or in Muse Code.

In Standard mode, your content — the prompts, code, files, and context you send, plus the model responses you get back — is not used to train Meta models. Muse Code subscribers can also use Contributor mode, which is on by default: it gives you more usage in exchange for letting Meta use your content to train future Meta models, and you can turn it off at any time in your settings. For Muse Wonder, Contributor mode isn't available on pay-as-you-go. See [Pricing and rate limits](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/pricing-rate-limits) for rates.

# Muse Spark

Muse Spark is Meta's model for agentic and coding work at scale, such as multi-step tool loops, software engineering assistants, and long-context reasoning. It costs less than Muse Wonder, and on Model API it also offers a discounted Contributor mode.

## At a glance

|                                                                                                |                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **[Standard mode](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/pricing-rate-limits#standard-mode) model IDs**      | `muse-spark-1.3`, `muse-spark-1.2`, `muse-spark-1.1`                                                                                                                                        |
| **[Contributor-mode](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/pricing-rate-limits#contributor-mode) variants** | `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, `muse-spark-1.2-contributor`                                                                                                                                  |
| **Input**                                                                                      | Text, image, video, audio, and PDF                                                                                                                                                          |
| **Output**                                                                                     | Text                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **Context window**                                                                             | 1,048,576 tokens                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **[Reasoning effort](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/reasoning)**                                     | `"minimal"` to `"max"` on `muse-spark-1.3`; see [Versions](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-spark#versions). The default is `"high"`                                                           |
| **Endpoints**                                                                                  | [Responses](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/protocols/responses), [Chat Completions](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/protocols/chat-completions), [Messages](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/protocols/messages) |
| **Pricing**                                                                                    | Pay-as-you-go; see [Muse Spark pricing](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/pricing-rate-limits#muse-spark-pricing)                                                                                    |
| **Rate limits**                                                                                | See [rate limits](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/pricing-rate-limits#rate-limits)                                                                                                                 |

## Build with Muse Spark

Use Muse Spark for agentic and coding work that needs strong reasoning at a lower cost than Muse Wonder:

- **Agent main loops**: run the main loop of an agent or assistant, and hand high-volume subtasks to [Muse Ember](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-ember).
- **Multi-step tool loops**: plan and drive tool calls across many turns.
- **Knowledge-heavy questions**: answer questions that depend on broad knowledge, without a retrieval step.
- **Coding assistants**: connect the [coding agent](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/coding-agents) you already use, or run [Muse Code](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code).

Muse Spark also handles [image understanding](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/media-understanding#images), [video](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/media-understanding#video) and [audio](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/media-understanding#audio) understanding, [tool calling](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/tool-calling), [structured output](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/structured-output), and [search grounding](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/search-grounding). For complex, long-running tasks where capability matters more than cost, see [Choose a model](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/choose-a-model).

## Versions

Muse Spark comes in three versions. All take text, image, video, audio, and PDF input, return text, and have a 1,048,576-token context window. They differ by capability:

- **Muse Spark 1.3** (`muse-spark-1.3`): the latest version, tuned for agentic workflows (multi-step tool, browser, and long-horizon tasks) with improved coding over 1.2. Supports all [reasoning effort](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/reasoning) levels, including the `"max"` level for extended reasoning (not available with `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`). **Recommended for new work.**
- **Muse Spark 1.2** (`muse-spark-1.2`): the previous version.
- **Muse Spark 1.1** (`muse-spark-1.1`): the original version.

> **NOTE: Audio input on Muse Spark 1.3**
>
> Audio understanding in Muse Spark 1.3 is not fully supported, and response quality for requests that include audio may be degraded. For audio, use Muse Spark 1.2, or [Muse Voice Transcribe](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/models#muse-voice-transcribe) for dedicated speech-to-text.

`muse-spark-1.3` is the default model in most code examples in these docs. The [coding agents](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/coding-agents), [agent frameworks](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/agent-frameworks), and [computer use](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/computer-use) guides use `muse-wonder-1.0` for long-running agentic work.

| Muse Spark 1.2 (`muse-spark-1.2`)                         | Standard mode             | Pay-as-you-go and [every plan](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/subscriptions#about) |

In [Standard mode](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/pricing-rate-limits#standard-mode), your content — the prompts, code, files, and context you send, plus the model responses you get back — is not used to train Meta models. # Muse Ember

Muse Ember is the efficient execution model in the Muse family, built for high-volume, repeated work. It runs the sub-agent tasks, tool calls, and routing inside larger agent workflows, and processes large collections of images, files, and records. Pair it with Muse Spark or Muse Wonder: the larger model plans, and Muse Ember handles the volume.

## At a glance

|                                                                                          |                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **[Standard mode](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/pricing-rate-limits#standard-mode) model ID** | `muse-ember-1.0`                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **Input**                                                                                | Text, image, video, audio, and PDF                                                                                                                                                          |
| **Output**                                                                               | Text                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **Context window**                                                                       | 1,048,576 tokens                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **Max output**                                                                           | 524,288 tokens                                                                                                                                                                              |
| **[Reasoning effort](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/reasoning)**                               | `"minimal"` to `"max"`; the default is `"max"`                                                                                                                                              |
| **Endpoints**                                                                            | [Responses](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/protocols/responses), [Chat Completions](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/protocols/chat-completions), [Messages](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/protocols/messages) |
| **Pricing**                                                                              | Pay-as-you-go, with long-context rates for requests over 200K input tokens; see [Muse Ember pricing](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/pricing-rate-limits#muse-ember-pricing)                       |
| **Rate limits**                                                                          | See [rate limits](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/pricing-rate-limits#rate-limits)                                                                                                                 |

## Build with Muse Ember

Use Muse Ember for bounded work that repeats many times:

- **Sub-agent tasks**: run the focused coding tasks, terminal commands, and lookups that a main agent hands out.
- **Tool calls**: drive tool calls inside a larger workflow, where cost and latency per call add up.
- **Routing**: classify requests and send each one to the right handler or model.
- **Work across large collections**: run the same task over thousands of images, files, or records, such as captioning and sorting photos, extracting fields, or classifying tickets, with many Muse Ember requests running in parallel.

Muse Ember accepts the same request body as Muse Spark, so switching most examples is a model ID change. [Switch between models](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/choose-a-model#switch-models) lists what differs. It works with [computer use](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/computer-use), [image understanding](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/media-understanding#images), [tool calling](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/tool-calling), [structured output](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/structured-output), and [search grounding](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/search-grounding).

For hard single-shot coding problems, knowledge-heavy questions, or visual coding, use Muse Spark or Muse Wonder. See [Choose a model](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/choose-a-model).

## Pair Muse Ember with a larger model

In an agent, run Muse Wonder or Muse Spark on the main loop to plan and reason, and hand repeated subtasks to Muse Ember. The reasoning models accept the same request body, so each request picks its model with the `model` field. [Combine models in one agent](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/choose-a-model#combine-models) shows how to set this up in the harnesses you already use.

## Make your first call

Send a request to the [Responses API](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/protocols/responses) with your `MODEL_API_KEY`:

```shell
curl -X POST "https://api.meta.ai/v1/responses" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MODEL_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
  "model": "muse-ember-1.0",
  "input": "Classify this support ticket as billing, bug, or feature request, and give a one-sentence reason: \"I was charged twice for my October invoice.\""
}'
```

For the same call in Python or TypeScript, follow the [quickstart](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/quickstart#first-call) and set the model to `muse-ember-1.0`.

## Availability

Muse Ember is on Model API and in [Muse Code](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code), on pay-as-you-go and with any subscription.

| Model                         | Model API (pay-as-you-go) | Muse Code                                                                              |
| :---------------------------- | :------------------------ | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Muse Ember (`muse-ember-1.0`) | Standard mode             | Pay-as-you-go and [every plan](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/subscriptions#about) |

On Model API, Muse Ember runs in [Standard mode](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/pricing-rate-limits#standard-mode) only; it has no Contributor-mode variant. A request with more than 200K input tokens, such as one with a long conversation history, is billed at higher long-context rates. See [Muse Ember pricing](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/pricing-rate-limits#muse-ember-pricing) for both tiers. On a Muse Code subscription, a request with more than 200K input tokens uses your plan's usage faster.

# Muse Spark Open

Muse Spark Open is the open-weight release of Muse Spark, Meta's agentic and coding model. Run it two ways:

- **Self-host:** download a checkpoint and serve it on your own GPUs with SGLang, vLLM, or another [runtime](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-spark-open/deploy#self-host), so every prompt and response stays inside your infrastructure.
- **Hosted provider:** call it through a [hosted provider's](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-spark-open/deploy#hosted-providers) API, with no GPUs to provision.

## Model variants

| Model           | Parameters             | Architecture                                                                             | Context window   |
| --------------- | ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| Muse Spark Open | 816B total, 42B active | Sparse mixture of experts, multimodal (text, image, audio, and video input; text output) | 1,048,576 tokens |

## Architecture

Muse Spark Open is a sparse mixture-of-experts transformer with built-in perception encoders. Each token routes to a small subset of experts, so per-token compute tracks the 42B active parameters. Serving still loads the full 816B weights into VRAM, which sets the hardware footprint.

## Supported languages

Muse Spark Open was trained on data from more than 100 languages.

## Checkpoints and hardware

Muse Spark Open ships in two checkpoint formats:

- **BF16:** the full-precision reference, about 1.65 TB of weights. Serves on eight GPUs, such as 8 × B300.
- **NVFP4:** stores most weights in 4-bit and keeps some layers in BF16, about 537 GB of weights. Serves on a single 4-GPU NVIDIA Blackwell node.

Serving needs memory beyond the weights for the key-value cache, activations, and runtime overhead: budget roughly 2 TB of VRAM for BF16. [Get the model](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-spark-open/get-the-model) has the download, and [Hardware platforms](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-spark-open/hardware-platforms) covers the NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel configurations, with sample commands.

# Muse Glimmer

[Muse Glimmer](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/models#muse-glimmer) is Meta's 30-billion-parameter open-source multimodal model, distilled from [Muse Spark](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/models#muse-spark) and built for local agentic workflows. Run it on your own hardware through supported runtimes. It ships with open weights, reads text and images, and reasons step by step before it answers.

Point your existing tooling at a local Muse Glimmer server and keep building — you own the weights, the runtime, and the data.

## Model variants

| Model        | Parameters | Architecture                                        | Context window                                    |
| ------------ | ---------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| Muse Glimmer | 30B        | Dense, multimodal (text + image input; text output) | 128K tokens by default; longer contexts supported |

## Architecture

Muse Glimmer is a dense, decoder-only multimodal transformer with a built-in vision encoder. It is trained from Muse Spark's outputs rather than from scratch. It accepts text and image input, produces text output, and has a default context window of 128K tokens with support for longer contexts.

## Supported languages

Muse Glimmer was trained on data from more than 100 languages.
